review.summary: Phase 9 is a docs/governance-only plan phase, and the plan is unusually precise and internally consistent: the eleven new routes are exactly eleven, the "six mutations" arithmetic (PUT runtime-profile + POST regenerate + four overrides) checks out, and every compatibility claim I could test against real code is true — the frozen 0.7.75 dataplane spec contains exactly 36 operations (contracts/sources/pan-dev/.../dp-openapi.yaml, 36 operationIds) matching the plan's "36 existing"; /v1/metering/quota is POST upstream with a data-plane GET compatibility helper (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/facade.rs:199-220) exactly as the plan excludes; the HTTP-422-only metadata fallback (facade.rs:118-138), the v1 download_report JSON return (reports.rs:290-310), the facade placement of error-log reads (facade.rs:221-238), bounded send_bytes (engine.rs:1094) and the pinned js-yaml (tools/package-lock.json:616-618) all exist as described. The check evidence is genuine and gate-bound: docs/checks/phase-09.json records passed=true, source_unchanged=true, source_sha256 2a6d220a… equal to the reviewed hash, and its two commands equal commands_for(9) (tools/check_phase.py:55-57), which tools/review_phase.py:99-113 enforces before generating the prompt I received — so the governance machinery actually ran and phases 1-8 predecessor evidence validated. verify-contracts.py passing also proves the frozen corpus and manifest set are untouched (tools/verify-contracts.py:417-418). What keeps this below the bar is evidence and settlement quality rather than ambition. The phase's own milestone is "Pin source identity", yet the pin exists only as prose (plan:16-23): the 0.93.0 spec is not in the repository, no machine-readable pin record or retrieval receipt was preserved, and network access is prohibited, so the entire quantitative core (47 = 36 + 11, the per-route schemas, the enumerated schema deltas) is unverifiable at this source and nothing in-repo would detect a phase-10 drift to a different revision. Two design points are also left genuinely ambiguous and would steer phase 10 wrong: whether current-spec required-field validation gates requests only or also responses (plan:106-108 contradicts plan:107's older-deployment tolerance), and a blanket rule to keep public parameters the spec no longer declares while silently dropping them on the wire (plan:65-67), which can hand a caller unfiltered results for a filter they explicitly passed. Finally, the executed gate is a whitespace check plus a frozen-corpus check: it exercises none of the governance tooling this phase modified, and the new docs/*.md file falls under an existing docs-wide assertion (tools/test_ci.py:220) that was not run. The required fixes are small and local to docs/governance.

findings.description: The phase-9 milestone is "Pin source identity", but the pin (pan.dev revision afef9d08030a56e18a04ea078f589313f1fa2b0c, 225109 bytes, SHA256 77f015de…) exists only in Markdown prose. The spec file is not in the repository (only the frozen 0.7.75 copy at contracts/sources/pan-dev/openapi-specs/prisma-airs-redteam/data-plane/dp-openapi.yaml exists), no retrieval receipt was preserved under docs/checks/, and no machine-readable record carries the provenance fields the repository already uses elsewhere (contracts/manifest.json:1845-1859 records repository/commit/upstreamPath/sha256/gitBlobSha1/bytes/license). Consequently nothing in-repo can detect a phase-10 retrieval of a different revision, and every quantitative claim in the plan — the 47-operation denominator (lines 12-14), the eleven routes, the enumerated schema deltas — is prose-only at this reviewed source. docs/PHASES.md:7 and the review prompt both require verifiable artifacts over completion prose.
findings.required_fix: Add a machine-readable pin record in this phase (e.g. docs/checks/phase-09-vendor-source-pin.json) carrying repository, commit, upstreamPath, sourceUrl, sha256, bytes, license and retrievedAt, reference it from the plan, and state in the Phase 10 gate row (line 143) that the committed source bytes must be compared byte-for-byte against that record and that the ledger must recount the operation denominator from the committed source, failing (not silently adapting) if it is not 47.

findings.description: The compatibility design is self-contradictory about validation direction. Line 107 requires newly introduced fields on existing response models to stay optional "to decode older deployments", while lines 106-108 require the current vendor wire validator not to be weakened and to "validate current required fields before model decoding". If that validation also applies to responses, a response from an older service deployment that omits a field 0.93.0 marks required will be rejected before the tolerant decoder ever runs, so the stated older-deployment tolerance is dead. If it applies only to requests, the tolerance holds but the sentence is misleading. Phase 10 implements both namespaced validators and additive model fields from this text, so the ambiguity will be resolved by guesswork.
findings.required_fix: State explicitly whether current-spec required-field validation gates requests only, or requests and responses. If responses are validated, define the documented behavior for older deployments missing newly required fields (which rule wins, what error or tolerance applies) and require a test for that case; if requests only, reword lines 106-108 to say so.

findings.description: "For parameters the spec no longer declares, preserve the source-level option but omit it on the dataplane wire and document the compatibility change" is a blanket rule that silently discards caller intent. For a load-bearing filter or scope parameter, accepting the argument and not sending it means the caller receives a broader result set than requested while the call appears to succeed — a correctness and data-exposure risk, not just a documentation matter. The plan correctly keeps the still-declared deprecated `threat` filters (line 68) and correctly forbids sending unsupported convenience parameters (line 66), but it never distinguishes cosmetic parameters from semantically load-bearing ones, and nothing requires the caller to learn that their filter was dropped.
findings.required_fix: Require Phase 10 to enumerate every existing parameter the pinned spec no longer declares and assign a per-parameter disposition: hard validation error before transport for parameters whose omission changes returned data (filters, scopes, limits), documented accepted no-op only for cosmetic ones. Require one test per parameter and a CHANGELOG entry per behavior change; remove the blanket silent-omission rule.

findings.description: The phase-9 command set is ["git","diff","--check"] and ["python","tools/verify-contracts.py"]. Neither exercises what this phase actually changed. This phase modifies the gate tool itself (tools/check_phase.py) and docs/PHASES.md, yet tools/test_review_phase.py (which imports commands_for) and tools/test_ci.py are not run, and CI still runs only "--phase 8 --verification-only" (tools/test_ci.py:82,308), so the new phase-9 branch and the governance invariants are unexecuted for this source. The new plan document also falls under an existing docs-wide assertion over sorted(docs/*.md) at tools/test_ci.py:220-227; I confirmed by reading that the plan text does not match the obsolete-publication patterns, but the gate did not verify it. Also note `git diff --check` does not inspect untracked files, so the phase's primary deliverable (the untracked plan document) is not covered even by the whitespace check.
findings.required_fix: Extend commands_for(9) to include ["python","-m","unittest","discover","-s","tools","-p","test_review_phase.py","-v"] and the same for test_ci.py (plus test_auxiliary_evidence.py if it asserts over docs/ or review bookkeeping), rerun tools/check_phase.py --phase 9 so the recorded command set matches, and request a fresh review against the resulting source fingerprint.

findings.description: The governance phase table stops at phase 8 and the "Milestone records" checklist (lines 26-33) likewise enumerates only 1-8, while docs/phase-status.json:1799-1826 now defines phases 9-12 as the active and pending phases. docs/PHASES.md:24 states that "The detailed checklist below determines implemented scope", so for phases 9-12 the authoritative scope determinant is absent from the authoritative document and lives only in the referenced plan (lines 46-54 point to it, which is why this is low rather than higher).
findings.required_fix: Add table rows and milestone-record entries for phases 9-12 in docs/PHASES.md with their milestones and acceptance evidence, referencing docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md:140-145 as the detailed checklist.

findings.description: The V2 download row requires a "Required typed `FileFormat`", but `FileFormat` already exists as an open, non_exhaustive enum with an `Unknown(String)` variant (crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:34966-34972, re-exported at crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team.rs:53). The plan's general rule is that "request enum validation remains strict where the vendor declares an enum" (line 117-118), which conflicts with passing an open enum carrying arbitrary caller strings into a query parameter; the existing v1 method guards this with common::filter on a &str (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/reports.rs:299). The verification list mentions "V2 format validation" (line 172) without saying what is rejected.
findings.required_fix: State in the plan that `FileFormat::Unknown` is rejected before credentials and transport for get_download_url (and any other request-position use of a shared open enum), while the enum stays open for response decoding, and make that rejection an explicit verification item.

findings.description: The generation design relies on js-yaml as a transitive dependency: it is declared only as a "^4.1.0" range inside @apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser (tools/package-lock.json:25) and resolved to 4.3.2 (tools/package-lock.json:616-618); tools/package.json:6-12 declares only swagger-parser, @types/node, tsx, typescript and zod. Requiring js-yaml from tooling depends on flat npm hoisting and on swagger-parser continuing to depend on it, so the canonical-JSON-vs-YAML verification can break for reasons unrelated to this project. "Pinned" is accurate only by way of the lockfile.
findings.required_fix: Declare an exact js-yaml version as a direct development dependency in tools/package.json (or state the exact resolved version in the plan and add a tooling assertion that the resolved version matches the recorded pin), so the YAML verification path does not depend on another package's transitive graph.

findings.description: The phase-9 entry records only id, name, status and plan. Phases 1-8 each carry scope_evidence, limitations and milestone blocks, and docs/PHASES.md:5 requires recording the review artifact, reviewed source state, checks, limitations and outcome. Nothing currently links phase 9 to its check report (docs/checks/phase-09.json), its scoped command set, or the governance documents it changed, so the progress source of truth is thinner for the active phase than for completed ones.
findings.required_fix: Add scope_evidence to the phase-9 entry listing docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md, docs/PHASES.md, tools/check_phase.py and docs/checks/phase-09.json, and record the scoped-check rationale (docs/governance-only) plus any accepted limitations alongside the review once it is accepted.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-09.json:2-6 records phase 9, source_sha256 2a6d220a501bbb6c3164f9777af6e6b4f4fec3b11af6ed4d96b3e22d99575c90 (equal to the reviewed source hash in the prompt), source_unchanged true and passed true.

docs/checks/phase-09.json:9-39 contains exactly two executed checks — git diff --check (exit 0) and /usr/bin/python tools/verify-contracts.py (exit 0, status "verified", baseline 0.34.0, commit 4a80dbdb…) — and both match commands_for(9) at tools/check_phase.py:55-57.

tools/review_phase.py:99-113 (check_evidence) requires phase, passed, matching source_sha256, source_unchanged and exact command-set equality before a prompt is generated; tools/review_phase.py:205-221 generates the prompt I received verbatim, so the recorded report was validated for this exact source.

tools/review_phase.py:43-60 excludes only docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json from the fingerprint, so docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md and docs/PHASES.md are bound to the reviewed hash; tools/review_phase.py:145-153 validated phases 1-8 accepted-review evidence before this review was requested.

tools/verify-contracts.py:417-418 enforces exact set equality between manifested and actual files under contracts/{fixtures,sources,licenses}, so the passing run proves no vendor 0.93.0 source was added or frozen source altered in this phase.

contracts/sources/pan-dev/openapi-specs/prisma-airs-redteam/data-plane/dp-openapi.yaml:5 is version 0.7.75 and contains exactly 36 operationIds across 35 paths, consistent with the plan's "36 have existing native methods" (docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md:12-14).

contracts/sources/pan-dev/openapi-specs/prisma-airs-redteam/data-plane/dp-openapi.yaml:901-907 shows /v1/metering/quota is POST upstream, and crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/facade.rs:198-220 shows get_quota (POST) plus the data-plane GET get_quota_summary helper — exactly the exclusion stated at plan line 122-123. The only other extra facade methods (get_management_languages at facade.rs:269-280, get_dashboard_overview at facade.rs:313-325) use the management plane, which the plan excludes at line 14.

Verified plan compatibility claims against code: HTTP-422-only metadata fallback with one absolute budget (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/facade.rs:118-138); v1 download_report returns JsonValue and never follows the URL (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/reports.rs:290-310); error-log reads live on the RedTeamClient facade (facade.rs:221-256), matching the plan's RedTeamClient::download_error_logs placement; bounded send_bytes exists (crates/scm-sdk/src/engine.rs:1094); all named client families exist (RedTeamScansClient, RedTeamReportsClient, RedTeamCustomAttackReportsClient, RedTeamClient facade).

Plan internal consistency: the new-operation table (plan:38-50) has exactly eleven rows, and the six mutations named at plan:168 (PUT runtime-profile, POST regenerate, four override routes) match that table.

docs/phase-status.json:3-4 sets active_phase 9 with the 47-operation completion target; docs/phase-status.json:1799-1826 defines phases 9-12; docs/PHASES.md:46-54 states phase 9 is a plan review gated at >=9/10 with no blocker/high findings, which matches tools/review_phase.py:92.

docs/implementation-plan.md:24 already anticipates that "After initial parity, Rust evolves against pinned vendor contracts", and docs/implementation-plan.md:125 sets the 0.x patch/breaking policy the plan's 0.1.1-or-0.2.0 decision (plan:190-193) follows, so no implementation-plan change is required for this follow-up.

tools/package.json:6-12 and tools/package-lock.json:25,616-618 confirm js-yaml 4.3.2 is present only as a transitive dependency of @apidevtools/swagger-parser, qualifying the plan's "pinned js-yaml transitive dependency" claim at plan:96-97.

crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:34966-34972 shows the pre-existing FileFormat enum is non_exhaustive with an Unknown(String) variant, relevant to the plan's "Required typed FileFormat" at plan:50.
limitations: The pinned Prisma AIRS Red Teaming dataplane 0.93.0 specification is not present in the repository and network access is prohibited, so I could not verify the pinned revision, the 225109-byte size, the SHA256 77f015de…, the 47/36/11 operation denominators, or any per-route schema, status-code, bound or enum claim in the plan. Those claims are reviewed only for internal consistency and for consistency with the frozen 0.7.75 spec and existing code.

Only Read/Glob/Grep were available: I could not compute file hashes, so the prompt's check-report hash 2def462a… is taken from tools/review_phase.py's own computation at prompt-generation time rather than independently recomputed, and I could not run git diff to prove the working-tree change set is docs/governance-only. I corroborated that indirectly from the git status snapshot, the passing contract-corpus set-equality check, and reading the red-team crate sources.

Phase 9's recorded evidence contains only two commands. No Rust compilation, test, generation-reproducibility, packaging, export-probe or tooling unit-test suite was executed for this source; all phase 1-8 check reports are historical records bound to earlier source fingerprints and were not re-executed here.

I judged only phase 9's acceptance criteria (pin identity, cover the eleven new and existing operations, settle compatibility/security/verification/release scope, docs-only change). The phase 10-12 deliverables are unimplemented by design and were not scored.
Per the prompt I did not read credential or tenant-registration material and stayed inside the repository; .local/ copies were only listed, not relied on as evidence.
